palace_department_registers.observation: Separate bureaus of the palace keep their own tablets for fields, flocks, workshops, chariots and rations.
palace_department_registers.ability_reason: Each palace bureau keeps registers of land, herds, workshops and rations; the palace can direct a whole province's labor and stores.
palace_department_registers.social_consequence: The palace sees every sheep and furrow, and every household answers to a register

envoy_inviolability.observation: An envoy may not be touched on the road or at court, even by a ruler at war with his master.

vassal_loyalty_oaths.observation: Lesser rulers swear before the god to hold the overlord's friends as friends and his enemies as enemies.

material_allotment_ledgers.observation: The palace weighs out bronze, wool and ivory to each workshop and records what must come back.
material_allotment_ledgers.social_consequence: Craftsmen work to the palace's allotment, and owe it whatever falls short

deposited_treaty_copies.observation: Each side keeps a copy of the treaty in its god's house, where breaking it is an offence to the god.

village_quota_collectors.observation: Village stewards answer for a fixed quota of grain, oil and linen, and make up any shortfall themselves.
village_quota_collectors.social_consequence: Stewards squeeze their neighbours to meet the palace's number

treaty_hostage_exchange.observation: Sons of each ruling house live at the other's court as pledges that the treaty will hold.

royal_inquiry_commissions.observation: The ruler sends trusted men to ask how a governor's stores went missing, and to name who took them.

village_self_rule_after_collapse.observation: The palace burned and its scribes scattered, but the village elders still keep the fields, the stores and the peace.
village_self_rule_after_collapse.ability_reason: When the palace fails, villages keep order, stores and fields under their own elders, and the collapse stops at their boundary.
village_self_rule_after_collapse.social_consequence: Villages lose the palace's reach and trade, but keep their own counsel

warrior_acclamation_assembly.observation: Free fighters gather under arms and choose their war leader by shouting and clashing their shields.

shrine_league_confederation.observation: Settlements that share a god's shrine swear to keep peace among themselves and to defend the shrine together.
shrine_league_confederation.ability_reason: Towns bound to one shrine keep peace with each other and defend it together; a league acts where no single town could.
shrine_league_confederation.social_consequence: Member towns give up the right to raze one another and send delegates to the shrine council

monthly_provisioning_districts.observation: Each district feeds the court for one month of the year, by turns, from its own stores.

noble_council.observation: The heads of the leading warrior houses meet as a council, and the leader acts only with their consent.

royal_covenant_charter.observation: The ruler swears before the god to keep the people's customs, and his rule holds only while he keeps the oath.

priestly_anointing.observation: The god's servants pour oil on the chosen ruler, and he rules as one the god has marked.

licensed_court_critics.observation: Certain seers may rebuke the ruler to his face in the god's name, and are not punished for it.

charter_colonies.observation: A new settlement is founded under a charter from the mother town that fixes its founder, laws, land shares and duties.

annual_elected_magistrates.observation: Magistrates are chosen each year for a fixed term, and the year is named for the chief of them.
annual_elected_magistrates.ability_reason: Magistrates hold office for one year at a time; no one keeps power long enough to make it his own.
annual_elected_magistrates.social_consequence: Leading families compete every year for office, and old grudges are settled at the election

foreign_consul_hosts.observation: A citizen is appointed to host the foreigners of one land, speak for them in court and see their contracts kept.

term_limit_laws.observation: No man may hold the same office again until ten years have passed.
term_limit_laws.social_consequence: Experienced men must step aside, and the town trades skill in office for safety from tyrants

intent_graded_homicide_law.observation: Courts tell killing on purpose from killing by mischance, and punish each differently.

debt_bondage_ban.observation: No citizen may be seized as a slave for debt; loans are secured on goods, not on bodies.
debt_bondage_ban.social_consequence: Lenders grow wary and credit tightens, but no citizen sells himself for a loan

property_class_franchise.observation: Citizens are ranked by the size of their harvest, and only the higher ranks may hold the great offices.

citizen_jury_courts.observation: Hundreds of citizens chosen by lot hear each case and vote with pebbles, too many to bribe.
citizen_jury_courts.social_consequence: Every citizen may sit in judgment, and many days go to the courts instead of the fields

divided_provincial_powers.observation: In each province the governor, the tax officer and the garrison commander answer separately to the ruler, and watch one another.

majority_vote_assembly.observation: The citizens vote by show of hands, and what the majority decides binds the whole town.
majority_vote_assembly.ability_reason: The assembly's counted vote binds the town: laws, war and peace are decided by the citizens themselves.
majority_vote_assembly.social_consequence: The minority must bow to a counted vote, and ambitious speakers learn to court the crowd

term_limited_emergency_office.observation: In a crisis one man may rule alone, but for six months only, and then he must lay the power down.

lot_chosen_council.observation: A council chosen by lot from every district prepares the assembly's business, and is replaced each year.

commoners_veto_tribunes.observation: Officers of the common people may halt any magistrate's act with a single word.
commoners_veto_tribunes.social_consequence: The commons gain a shield, and public business can stall for months

ostracism_vote.observation: Once a year the citizens may scratch a name on sherds; the man named most must leave for ten years.

league_common_treasury.observation: League members pay assessed shares into a common treasury at the shrine, for ships and defence.
league_common_treasury.social_consequence: The weaker members pay while the leading town decides how the money is spent

end_of_term_audits.observation: No magistrate may leave office until auditors have checked every coin and measure of grain he handled.

paid_civic_duty.observation: Jurors and councillors are paid a day's wage, so poor men can serve as well as rich ones.

inscribed_treasury_accounts.observation: The treasury's receipts and payments are cut in stone where every citizen may read them.

auctioned_public_contracts.observation: Road works and tax collection are let by auction to the highest bidder, who then profits as he can.
auctioned_public_contracts.social_consequence: Contractors grow rich squeezing taxpayers for more than they bid

unlawful_decree_challenge.observation: Any citizen may prosecute the man who proposed a decree that breaks the laws, even after it has passed.

risk_pools.observation: Lenders advance money on a ship and its cargo and forfeit it if the ship is lost, so many small shares spread the risk.

market_wardens.observation: Elected wardens walk the market checking weights, measures and the quality of bread and grain.

written_court_procedure.observation: Charges, answers, witnesses and the time for speeches are fixed in writing, and a water-clock times each side.

commissioned_lawgivers.observation: A town in strife invites a wise man from elsewhere to write all its laws anew.

bail_guarantors.observation: Friends stand as guarantors for an accused man, and he stays free until his trial.

comparative_constitutions.observation: Scholars gather the constitutions of many towns and compare how each one rules itself.

district_royal_banks.observation: Royal banks in each district receive taxes, pay officials and record every transfer by written order.

federal_proportional_league.observation: League members vote by size in a federal council and send soldiers in proportion.

legal_jurisconsults.observation: Men learned in the law advise judges and parties, and their opinions are copied and cited.

foreigners_court.observation: A separate magistrate hears cases between foreigners and citizens, judging by fairness instead of the town's own rites.

realm_wide_standardization.observation: One set of weights, one script and one axle width are decreed for every province of the realm.
realm_wide_standardization.ability_reason: One set of weights, one script and one axle width across the realm: taxes, trade and carts pass every province alike.
realm_wide_standardization.social_consequence: Local scripts and measures are forbidden, and old provinces feel conquered twice

rotated_appointed_prefects.observation: Governors are appointed from the capital and moved to a new province every few years.
rotated_appointed_prefects.ability_reason: Appointed governors are rotated before they can root local power, and the provinces answer to the capital.
rotated_appointed_prefects.social_consequence: Provinces are ruled by strangers who never stay long enough to learn them

magistrate_edict_law.observation: Each year the incoming magistrate posts the rules he will follow, adapting the law to new kinds of case.

mixed_constitution_checks.observation: Magistrates, a council of elders and the assemblies each hold part of the power, and each can check the others.
mixed_constitution_checks.ability_reason: Power is shared among officers, elders and assemblies that check one another; no faction can seize the whole state.
mixed_constitution_checks.social_consequence: No faction can rule alone, and decisions come slower for it

extortion_court.observation: A standing court tries governors who robbed their provinces, and the guilty must repay double.

merit_recommendation.observation: Each district's notables send up men of known conduct and learning to serve as officials.

state_official_academy.observation: Young men study the classics at a state academy, and its graduates fill the offices.

written_office_examinations.observation: Candidates for office sit written examinations, and posts go to those who pass.
written_office_examinations.ability_reason: Posts go to candidates who pass written examinations, not only to the well-born; the realm is run by trained officials.
written_office_examinations.social_consequence: Office opens to talent, but only to talent schooled in the set texts

salt_iron_monopoly.observation: Only the state's works may boil salt or smelt iron, and the profits pay the frontier armies.
salt_iron_monopoly.social_consequence: The treasury fills while households pay more for salt and get worse iron tools

price_stabilizing_granary.observation: The state buys grain when it is cheap and sells it when it is dear, and famine prices are held down.

citizenship_extension.observation: Allied towns are granted citizenship, and their men vote, trade and serve as citizens.

public_credit.observation: The treasury borrows from the god's house and from wealthy citizens, and repays from future revenues.
public_credit.ability_reason: The treasury can borrow against future revenues for a war or a wall, and repay over years.
public_credit.social_consequence: Debts outlive the officials who contracted them, and future taxes are already spent

veiled_monarchy_offices.observation: One man holds every old office at once; the forms of the old constitution stay, but he decides.
veiled_monarchy_offices.social_consequence: Peace returns, and the assemblies' voice becomes a formality

universal_loyalty_oath.observation: Every province swears the same oath to the ruler and his house, on the same day each year.

military_pension_treasury.observation: A special treasury, fed by taxes on sales and inheritances, pays each soldier a lump sum at discharge.
military_pension_treasury.social_consequence: Veterans are provided for, and every sale and inheritance pays for it

binding_jurist_opinions.observation: The opinions of licensed jurists bind the courts, and judges follow the majority of them.

capped_advocate_fees.observation: Advocates' fees are capped by law, and a poor man can afford to be heard.

provincial_town_councils.observation: Councils of provincial towns meet each year and send their petitions and complaints to the ruler.

municipal_charters.observation: Towns govern themselves under charters, with elected councils and magistrates for roads, markets and courts.
municipal_charters.ability_reason: Chartered towns run their own roads, markets and courts under elected councils; the realm governs through self-governing towns.
municipal_charters.social_consequence: Town notables carry the cost of office and answer for their town's taxes

graded_land_tax.observation: Fields are measured and graded by their soil, and each grade pays its own fixed rate.

chartered_craft_associations.observation: Craftsmen's associations hold charters, keep a common chest and bury their members with honour.

professional_service.observation: Officials are salaried, ranked and promoted through a career, and serve whoever rules.
professional_service.ability_reason: Salaried officials in ranked careers keep procedure and records through every change of ruler.
professional_service.social_consequence: The offices outlast their holders and become a power of their own

petition_registers.observation: Petitions to the ruler are registered and answered in writing, and the reply is posted for all to read.

official_mandate_registers.observation: Every official's commission, powers and term are registered, and orders beyond them can be refused.

public_office_handover.observation: An outgoing official hands over the stores, records and pending cases to his successor by inventory.

universal_citizenship.observation: All free inhabitants of the realm become citizens under one law, and pay the citizens' taxes.
universal_citizenship.social_consequence: Old distinctions fade, and the new citizens owe the new taxes

nine_rank_official_grading.observation: Officials are graded in nine ranks, and the ranks soon follow family more than merit.
nine_rank_official_grading.social_consequence: Great families settle into the high ranks and pass them to their sons

annual_tax_budget.observation: Taxes are fixed each year from a set assessment cycle, and the needs of army and court are reckoned in advance.

shared_co_rulers.observation: Two or four rulers divide the realm, each with his own court and army, bound to one another by oath.
shared_co_rulers.social_consequence: Each court must be fed and garrisoned, and taxes rise to pay for them

civil_military_separation.observation: Governors keep the courts and the taxes; generals keep the troops, and neither commands the other.

compiled_rescript_code.observation: The ruler's written replies to officials and petitioners are collected into one code for every court.
compiled_rescript_code.ability_reason: The ruler's rulings are gathered into one code; every judge in the realm cites the same decisions.
compiled_rescript_code.social_consequence: The law becomes certain and uniform, and harder to change

shrine_arbitration_courts.observation: Parties may bring civil suits before the god's servants, whose judgment is swift and cheap.

town_advocate_for_poor.observation: Each town appoints an advocate to defend the poor against the exactions of officials.
